causal_chain: Context shows accepted frontier and known-good packages were resource-deferred, while earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off.

If gains do not appear, or if a generic hard-negative variant matches them without the predicted popularity-specific pattern, then the diagnosis that popularity-shaped contrast is the missing mechanism is weakened.

If the comparison distribution is the active cause, the modified model should outperform the matched BPR-MF control specifically through better discrimination against exposed-but-unconsumed head items and improved recovery of preference-consistent alternatives in full-sort ranking.
In pairwise BPR-MF, many ranking errors can arise because uniformly sampled negatives are too easy and do not force separation from highly exposed but unconsumed items.
Replacing uniform negatives with popularity-conditioned negatives changes only the training comparison distribution while preserving backbone, scorer, and evaluation.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any difference versus BPR_MF is caused only by generic stochastic hardening from changing the negative sampler, not by the popularity-specific mechanism; therefore a popularity-conditioned sampler should not show a distinctive advantage over either the matched control or a generic mixed-negative alternative on the predicted slices.
discriminative_predictions: A generic hard-negative alternative such as mixed negatives may change training difficulty, but it should not reproduce the same popularity-specific slice pattern if popularity exposure is the operative cause.

Against the competing explanation, popularity-conditioned negatives should show larger relative gains than plain BPR_MF on users whose candidate lists are dominated by popular items, not merely a uniform lift across all users.
If the mechanism is real, the gain pattern should be more consistent on head-item suppression and tail-or-mid popularity recovery than would be expected from generic sampling noise.
expected_evidence: Full-sort NDCG@10 exceeds the matched BPR_MF control under the frozen split.
Score separation between observed positives and popular unobserved items increases relative to the control.
The mechanism-off ablation reverting to uniform negatives removes most of the effect if the sampler is causal.
User or item popularity-stratified analysis shows a stronger effect where popular distractors are more prevalent.
blind_projection.falsifier: The proposal is falsified if popularity-conditioned negatives fail to improve over matched BPR_MF, or if a generic mixed-negative sampler matches or exceeds its effect without the predicted popularity-specific slice behavior.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This is intentionally a low-change, falsification-friendly wedge because the accepted context identifies the need for an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off rather than another composite mechanism. The change is restricted to the negative sampling operator so causal attribution is testable within the small qualification budget.
blind_projection.hypothesis: BPR_MF with popularity-conditioned negative sampling will outperform matched BPR_MF on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 because training against exposure-plausible popular negatives teaches the model to reject attractive but non-preferred head items that uniform negative sampling under-trains against.
implementation_requirements: Implement or enable a popularity-proportional negative sampler over training items using only train interactions.
Keep the BPR-MF scorer, embedding dimensionality, optimizer family, and evaluation pipeline matched to the control.
Log popularity-stratified diagnostics for sampled negatives and ranked outputs to support falsification.
Provide an executable mechanism-off path that switches the sampler back to uniform negatives without altering any other training component.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched BPR_MF control with identical backbone, parameterization, optimizer schedule, train-only fitting, and full-sort evaluation; the only difference allowed is uniform negatives in the control versus popularity-conditioned negatives in the treatment.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Change the pairwise training sampler from uniform item negatives to popularity-conditioned negatives while leaving the BPR-MF scoring function unchanged.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism off = identical BPR_MF training and evaluation with the popularity-conditioned sampler disabled and replaced by the standard uniform negative sampler.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A two-arm comparison between BPR_MF and BPR_MF__BPR_POPULARITY_NEGATIVE, with one additional diagnostic slice by user/item popularity, to test whether popularity-shaped negative exposure alone explains any ranking gain.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does popularity-conditioned negative sampling provide a causally attributable ranking benefit over matched BPR-MF, or are any apparent gains explainable by generic sampling difficulty alone?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: Because this proposal changes only the negative sampler on top of an already matched BPR_MF pipeline, it should fit within the existing qualification budget and is less resource-risky than deferred frontier composites.
